function_question: How does nature keep cool under a burning sun?

opening.text: There was a girl called Amara who knew every swing, climbing frame and hiding spot in her local playground.
Every afternoon, Amara helped the little kids take turns on the big shiny slide.
Then summer came. The slide got so hot that a little boy touched it and cried, "Ouch! It's burning!" Nobody could use it any more.

card.problem: The metal slide is too hot to use in summer
card.goal: Keep a surface cool in the sun

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: A slide nobody can use
chapters.line: Amara wonders: how can a slide stay cool in the blazing sun?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Amara needs a cool partner
chapters.line: A hot slide needs two cool heads. Will you join Amara?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Amara meet heroes that stay cool in burning heat.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of reflect, shade and radiate
chapters.line: The heroes share their three ways to beat the heat.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The thermometer race
chapters.line: Amara sets out four metal lids in the sun.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The playground empathy map
chapters.line: You already know what the kids say and do. Now find out what they think and feel.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every cool design starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The sun test
chapters.line: The first slide still warms up. You fix it, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Whoosh!
chapters.line: The little kids are back on the slide, laughing.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. The playground slide gets so hot in summer that nobody can use it. Can you help Amara keep it cool? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a spark of an idea for beating the heat. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been beating the heat for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who stay cool in the sun!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which lid will warm up the least in 20 minutes? Use a thermometer, never your hand.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your cool slide, with the sun and its rays, like a real designer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your cool slide and put it in the sun next to a bare tray. After 20 minutes, which one is cooler?
guide.retry_tip: Designers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, the playground slide stays cool all summer long, thanks to YOUR design, and the little kids never stop sliding.

quick_check.question: At 9 am the slide was 25 °C. By 2 pm it was 65 °C. How many degrees did it warm up?
quick_check.right: Right! 65 take away 25 is 40 degrees. That's a lot of heat from the sun!

clue_cards.name: Saharan silver ant
clue_cards.trick: Tiny triangle-shaped hairs that shine like silver.
clue_cards.does: They bounce sunlight away and help heat escape.

clue_cards.name: Desert snail
clue_cards.does: It reflects most of the sunlight, so the snail inside stays cooler.

clue_cards.name: African elephant
clue_cards.trick: Huge, thin ears full of blood vessels.
clue_cards.does: Flapping them lets heat escape from the blood.

clue_cards.name: Acacia tree
clue_cards.trick: A wide, flat top like an umbrella.
clue_cards.does: Its shade keeps the ground and animals below much cooler.

predict.prompt: Heats up fast or stays cooler in the sun? Predict first!
predict.explain: Dark colours soak up sunlight and turn it into heat. White things bounce much of it away, and shade stops it arriving at all.

lab.title: The hot-or-not thermometer race
lab.predict: Which lid will warm up the least after 20 minutes in the sun?

tool.name: Empathy Map
tool.intro: You already know S (Says) and D (Does) from the Empathy Map. Today you'll learn the last 2 boxes: Thinks and Feels. They're the hidden ones, so you have to watch and ask kindly.

parts.name: Thinks
parts.what: What might the person be thinking, even if they don't say it?
parts.example: 🥪 A kid thinks: "I hope my sandwich isn't squashed again."
parts.starter: Standing at the top of the hot slide, a little kid might think…

parts.name: Feels
parts.what: How does the person feel? Happy, scared, cross, left out?
parts.example: 🥪 They feel excited at lunchtime, then sad if their sandwich is soggy.
parts.starter: When the slide is too hot, the little kids feel…

sketch_checklist: I drew my slide from the side with the sun in the sky.
I drew arrows to show sunlight being reflected or blocked.
I labelled where heat can escape.

test.measure: temperature rise in °C after 20 minutes in the sun
test.check_question: Slide check: could a kid still slide down it safely?

reflection.question: Which nature trick kept your slide cool?
